title: SEC-000002: Bounded connection admission and per-service resource budget
statement: The BMS master software shall bound the resources consumed by any network service by enforcing, for every service, a hard cap on concurrently serviced connections, a finite receive timeout, a per-connection byte budget, and a deterministic close of any connection that exceeds its budget, and shall raise a diagnosis entry on every admission refusal and every budget breach.
rationale: A service with unbounded connection resources can be made to stop serving legitimate peers by a peer that requires no special capability. In the real source the relevant conditions are present in combination: the listen backlog is a compile-time constant of 1, the accept loop hands every accepted socket to a single-deep queue with a zero block time and discards the enqueue result, and the receive timeout is portMAX_DELAY, so a connected peer that sends nothing blocks its service task indefinitely. The requirement also requires the refusal to be diagnosable, because a silently discarded overflow cannot be distinguished from normal operation during field analysis (TARA threats THR-001, THR-003).

acceptance_criteria.measure: Connections simultaneously serviced by one service instance
Maximum time a service task may block in a receive call waiting for a peer that has sent nothing
Bytes a single connection may cause to be buffered before the connection is closed
Time from budget breach to the connection being closed and its resources released
Successful authenticated connections served per hour while a hostile peer holds the maximum permitted concurrent connections open and silent
Diagnosis entries raised per refused admission and per detected budget breach

safety_allocation.mitigation: Availability mitigation. The recorded impact of TARA threat THR-003 is currently bounded because the affected service is not on a safety path in the real source; this requirement exists so that the hypothetical project does not rely on that boundary once it adds a safety-relevant service.

standards_mappings.rationale: Named for traceability of intent only; no ISO/SAE 21434 work product exists and no conformance is claimed.
standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale says so in its own words ('named for traceability of intent only'): the clause is named for traceability or to record a boundary or an absence, and the record draws no content from the clause and claims nothing about it. The disposition is carried by `status`; the relationship is not a mapping from this record onto the clause.

standards_mappings.reference: Part 4, Clause 7 (availability of technical safety requirements)
standards_mappings.rationale: The hypothetical project has no resource-budget concept for communication services. This requirement is the proposed closure and it is unverified.
standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale states the derivation explicitly ('is the'): this record was written from the clause's concept, or supplies the work product the clause expects, or consumes the one the clause produces. The clause is the intellectual source of the content, which is what `derivation_basis` names. It is NOT a conformance claim: no clause text was consulted, no assessment was performed, and the clause is not a yardstick this record was measured against.

safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: This requirement belongs to the fictional reference project this corpus declares in its synthetic_reference profile, not to the foxBMS 2 product. foxBMS 2 published no requirement of any kind with an identifier, and nothing was ever allocated to an ASIL on its behalf. It is a forward-engineered proposal for a fictional item's resource budget, and its ISO mapping status is `gap`: the clause is named to record what does not exist, not to assert that something does.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees a safety-domain requirement with a connection cap, a receive timeout and a per-connection byte budget, mapped to ISO 26262 Part 4 Clause 7, will conclude the product bounds the resources its network services consume. The mapping is `relationship: referenced_only` with status `gap`, the asil is `not_applicable`, and the record's own rationale says the unbounded conditions are present in the source in combination - so this is a record of a defect, not of a control.

derivation_basis.locator: src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:241-294 (ETH_ListenForConnection) for the accept path and src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:128-239 (ETH_EchoServerInstance) for the service whose resource use is unbounded, with src/app/application/config/ethernet_cfg.h:84-96 (ETH_ECHO_SERVER_PORT_NUMBER) for the port it listens on. Pinned commit 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437. The caps themselves are the reference project's proposal; the source contains none of them.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the pinned source has no per-connection or per-service resource bound, which is a real and checkable observation and the reason the record is worth keeping. It supports nothing about the proposed caps being implemented, and the clause is named as a gap rather than as a standard the record meets.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. Forward-engineered security requirement 'bounded-connection-admission-resource-budget' for the synthetic_reference project. Derived from threat analysis FB2-SAF-TAR-000001.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: Added the asil_justification that the requirement applicability validator requires and did not find: this record marks safety_allocation.asil as not_applicable, which requirement.schema.json enumerates as the value for a requirement to which no ASIL determination applies, and the rule requires a recorded reason for that marking. The reason had been present only inside safety_allocation.mitigation and safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref, which are required on every requirement whatever its marking and are therefore populated identically on the ASIL_D records; they cannot serve as a justification specific to this marking. The new field states the reason on its own, names what the safety_goal_ref trace does and does not carry, and records the open items where the marking depends on something not yet established. The asil value, the statement, the mitigation, the safety_goal_ref and the revision-relevant content of the record are unchanged. Remediation of the requirement applicability validator finding raised by finding FB2-REV-FND-000032. Nothing in this field asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level or human approval; human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

revision_history.author: cybersecurity_engineer
revision_history.description: Added the fault_reaction block that the safety-requirement completeness validator (MUT-008, safety_requirement_completeness_checker) requires and did not find. That rule used to carry an id filter '-FSR-' in id which made it structurally incapable of reporting this record, while its sibling verification_traceability_checker selected the same population - requirement plus engineering_domain equals safety - with no id filter at all. The filter has been removed from the rule, which widened its scope and weakened nothing; see finding FB2-REV-FND-000039. The block authored here is transcribed from this record's own statement, acceptance_criteria and conditions_modes, and records three absences honestly rather than filling them: neither safety concept allocates a fault reaction to any element for the security chain (element_owns_reaction is therefore false), the safety goal's timing budget has no cybersecurity leg so no reaction-time budget is stated, and the control's real-source status and unverified verification leg are carried through. No acceptance criterion, ASIL value, statement, rationale, verification approach or verification status was changed. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human has approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.

revision_history.author: corpus_governance
revision_history.description: Added safety_class_disclaimer, carrying no modification of the statement, the ASIL value, the allocation, the acceptance criteria or any standards mapping. The defect corrected is legibility: this record was already marked `profile: synthetic_reference` and, for the SYRs, already says in its own limitations field that it establishes nothing about the real project - but a reader skimming `artifact_type`, `asil` and `standards_mappings` sees a safety requirement at an ASIL with an ISO 26262 clause and status `mapped`, and reads it as an allocated, conformant safety obligation of the product. It is a requirement of the fictional reference project this corpus declares. derivation_basis names what the derivation actually rests on - for most of these, specific pinned file:line ranges, and for FB2-SAF-FSR-000004, FB2-HW-TSR-000004, FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 and FB2-SYS-SYR-000005, the explicit statement that there is no such source because the subject does not exist - and states what it does not support. No other field of the record was modified.

real_source_presence: Control PARTIALLY PRESENT, and the partial presence is stated explicitly. Present: the receive into the service buffer is length-bounded — src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:157 declares uint8_t rxBuffer[ipconfigTCP_MSS] and :175 passes ipconfigTCP_MSS as the receive length, and :224 does the same on the drain path, so no read can exceed the array (TARA mitigation MIT-003, present_in_source). ABSENT: every admission control. src/app/application/config/ethernet_cfg.h:85 sets the backlog to 1, :94 sets the receive timeout to portMAX_DELAY, src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:292 discards the return value of the queue send, and no per-connection cap, idle timeout or deterministic close exists. Anchors FB2-SRC-COD-000058, FB2-SRC-COD-000062.
real_source_control_status_note: Part of the capability this requirement specifies is present in the real foxBMS 2 source and part is not; see real_source_presence for the itemised split.

fault_reaction.reaction: Refuse the admission, or close the connection deterministically. Both halves are the requirement's own text: the statement requires 'a deterministic close of any connection that exceeds its budget' and 'a diagnosis entry on every admission refusal and every budget breach'. The reaction is bounded resource consumption under a hostile peer - the cap is the reaction, and exceeding it terminates the connection rather than degrading the service.
fault_reaction.triggered_by: An inbound connection arriving when the service is already at its concurrent-connection cap; a service task blocking in a receive call past the finite receive timeout; a single connection buffering past its per-connection byte budget.
fault_reaction.diagnosis: One diagnosis entry per refused admission and one per detected budget breach. Transcribed from this record's own acceptance criterion 'Admission-refusal diagnosability / Diagnosis entries raised per refused admission and per detected budget breach / 1 / entry per event'.
fault_reaction.reaction_time_bound: 'Budget-breach response time / Time from budget breach to the connection being closed and its resources released / 100 ms'. Transcribed from this record's own acceptance criterion and the only reaction-time bound this record states. Two other figures in the record are the limits the reaction enforces rather than its own latency: the concurrent cap of 4 connections, the 2000 ms receive timeout and the 65536-byte per-connection budget.
fault_reaction.mode_dependence: Mode-independent on the reaction itself, and this is load-bearing rather than incidental. A resource-exhaustion reaction closes a connection; in DEGRADED and COMMISSIONING the same closure applies, and no mode in this record's conditions_modes (NORMAL, CHARGING, DISCHARGE, PRECHARGE, DEGRADED, COMMISSIONING) is granted an exemption. The one mode-sensitive consequence is recorded in this record's own acceptance criteria and is not a mode-dependent reaction: 'Service availability under exhaustion' requires at least one successful authenticated connection per hour while a hostile peer holds the maximum permitted concurrent connections open and silent, so a reaction that simply closed everything would fail the record's own criterion.
fault_reaction.allocation_basis: NO ELEMENT ALLOCATES A FAULT REACTION FOR THE SECURITY CHAIN. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001.safety_strategies.fault_reaction lists four reactions and allocates them to AR-002, AR-004, AR-005 and AR-006; FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.fault_reaction lists the same four. None of them is a reaction to a detected security attack, and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001.safety_strategies.fault_detection lists five detection mechanisms, none of which is a communication-integrity or authentication check. The security chain therefore has no element-level reaction budget anywhere in this corpus. That is a real gap and it is recorded as one rather than closed by inventing an allocation. The reaction this field states is the one this requirement's own statement mandates and the one its own acceptance criteria decide; who carries it technically, and within what time, is not derivable from any record that exists.
fault_reaction.budget_absence_note: No reaction_time_budget_ms is stated, and that is deliberate rather than an omission. The safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001.timing_budget.allocation has ten entries, none of which is a cybersecurity leg, and neither safety concept allocates one to the security chain, so there is no interval in this corpus against which a security reaction time could be checked. The decidable bounds that DO exist are stated in reaction_time_bound, transcribed from this record's own acceptance criteria. Inventing a millisecond figure here would create a number with nothing to verify it against, which is the failure mode finding FB2-REV-FND-000025 was raised about.
fault_reaction.derivation: Transcribed, not invented. reaction, triggered_by, diagnosis, reaction_time_bound and mode_dependence are each quoted or paraphrased from text this record already carried at revision 2: its own statement, its own acceptance_criteria and its own conditions_modes. The numeric bound in reaction_time_bound is a threshold this record's own acceptance criteria already stated; where the record states no such bound, this field says so rather than supplying one. No acceptance criterion, ASIL value, verification approach, verification_status, statement or rationale was altered by adding this field.
fault_reaction.unverified_leg_note: The verification leg is absent in the real source and the record says so: real_source_control_status is 'partially_present'. This block therefore describes what the requirement specifies, not what the foxBMS 2 product does. No measurement, no timing analysis and no injection campaign exists in this corpus for any part of it.
fault_reaction.open_limits: real_source_control_status on this record is 'partially_present', so part of the control exists in the real foxBMS 2 source and part does not; the record's own block states which is which, and this field does not restate it. The verification leg is a plan, not an outcome: verification_status is not_verified and verification_approach is the single word 'test'. The reaction has no element-level allocation in either safety concept, and the 100 ms budget above is a requirement threshold with no element, no measurement and no timing analysis behind it. Whether 100 ms is achievable on the target is not established anywhere in this corpus.

latent_defect_note: A separate, configuration-dependent latent defect is recorded in the TARA and is NOT addressed by this requirement: at src/app/application/ethernet/ethernet.c:189 the receive buffer is printed with a %s conversion although the buffer is not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated when a receive fills all ipconfigTCP_MSS bytes. Under the evidenced configuration this code is compiled out, because ipconfigHAS_DEBUG_PRINTF is not defined in the project's FreeRTOSIPConfig.h and therefore takes the default ipconfigDISABLE, which reduces FreeRTOS_debug_printf to a no-op (src/os/freertos/freertos-plus/freertos-plus-tcp/source/include/FreeRTOSIPConfigDefaults.h:3162-3176). No out-of-bounds read is therefore claimed to be reachable, and this requirement does not claim to fix it. Anchor FB2-SRC-COD-000075.

asil_justification.scope_of_this_classification: This field records why safety_allocation.asil is not_applicable on this requirement. It is a statement about this record's own allocation bookkeeping inside a fictional reference project. It is not a determination about the real foxBMS 2 product and not evidence about that product's availability posture.
asil_justification.reason: This requirement is classified 'security' and it bounds connection admission and the resource budget of a service. ISO 26262 does not allocate an ASIL to a security requirement, so not_applicable is the schema's own enumerated value for that case. The TARA entry THR-003 records the availability impact as currently bounded, and that bound is a property of the threat analysis, not of any ASIL determination.
asil_justification.open_item: The bound is contingent. The record states that the affected service is not on a safety path in the real source. If the project adds a safety-relevant service on the same path, the bound no longer holds and this requirement's classification would have to be revisited. This field does not claim the bound is durable.
what_this_does_not_assert: It does not assert conformity with ISO 26262, and it is not a certification, a type approval, or evidence of one. Nothing in this field was audited to produce it.

It does not assert human approval. human_approval_status on this record is pending, production_authorized is false and product_verification_credit is false, and no functional-safety expert has confirmed any of it.
It does not establish that any ASIL was correctly assigned to any safety requirement in this corpus. It explains only why this requirement is not itself an ASIL-allocated item.
It does not assert tool qualification. No tool used anywhere in this corpus has been qualified for a safety purpose.
It does not assert an ASPICE capability level for anything.
